1.explanation: 1. We define a small wrapper component DataTableGroup using Grommet’s Select. It shows a placeholder, an icon that flips when open, and a clear control.\n2. In the example, we keep a piece of state groupBy that holds the selected column object (property and header). 3. We pass groupByProp = [groupBy.property] to the DataTable’s groupBy prop; when groupBy is undefined the table is ungrouped. 4. Selecting an option in the DataTableGroup updates the state and re-renders the table grouped by that column. 5. This reproduces the missing DataTableGroup feature as demonstrated in the screenshots.
1.bug_scenario: In the app’s DataTable view, the user wants a small “Group by…” control (with a placeholder, clear button, and an icon) that drives the DataTable’s groupBy prop. In the screenshots you can see a Select dropdown listing all possible columns (Date, Time, Type, Source, Partition, Severity, etc.), the ability to clear the selection, and when a column is chosen the table groups its rows by that column. Currently there is no dedicated DataTableGroup component, so this example wires up a plain Grommet Select to DataTable’s groupBy state to reproduce the behavior.
